Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

optcompR 0.1.0

  • First release.
  • Modeling: continuous, integer and binary variables, parameters, vectorized linear, quadratic and nonlinear expressions with sparse Matrix support, ranged constraints and named blocks.
  • Classification into LP, MILP, QP, MIQP, QCQP, MIQCQP, SOCP, MISOCP, CONIC, NLP and MINLP with recorded convexity evidence, and capability-aware solver selection.
  • Backends: HiGHS (LP, MILP, convex QP, ranging, warm starts), SCIP (global MIQCQP and MISOCP, native indicator and SOS constraints), Clarabel (LP, convex QP and conic programs), OSQP (convex QP), NLopt SLSQP (local NLP), IPOPT with exact Hessians (compiled in when found with pkg-config), NLP branch and bound for MINLP, and ROI plugins.
  • Cone constraints (opt_soc_constraint(), opt_exp_cone(), opt_pow_cone(), opt_psd_constraint()) and symmetric matrix variables (opt_sym_variable()).
  • Indicator, SOS1, SOS2, complementarity and logical constraints with exact reformulations for solvers without native support.
  • Robust and stochastic optimization: opt_robust_constraint(), opt_chance_constraint(), opt_cvar(), opt_expectation(), opt_worst_expectation().
  • Derivatives of optimal solutions with respect to parameters (opt_solution_jacobian()).
  • ODE least squares losses for modelcompR models (opt_ode_loss()).
  • Results with standardized statuses, duals as derivatives of the optimal value, independent feasibility and KKT diagnostics (opt_check()).
  • Exact gradients, Jacobians and Lagrangian Hessians; external R functions with supplied, jaxR or labeled finite difference gradients (opt_function()).
  • Sensitivity ranging, fixed relaxations of MILPs and scenario sweeps.
  • Multiobjective scalarizations: opt_weighted(), opt_lexicographic(), opt_epsilon_constraint().
  • Exact feasibility checks and optimality certificates for LP and MILP through z3r (opt_z3_check(), opt_z3_certify()).
  • Conversion to and from symcompR expressions; MPS and LP export.
  • Twenty vignettes and a pkgdown site.
  • Correctness safeguards: binary variables keep 0/1 bounds whatever opt_set_bounds() sets; a smallest Hessian eigenvalue that is negative beyond rounding but inside the curvature tolerance makes convexity “unknown”, and convex-only solvers now require proven convexity; NLopt’s objective-target stop is "objective_limit"; OSQP and IPOPT points at a limit are reported feasible only after a feasibility check; IPOPT diverging iterates are no longer called unbounded; nlpbb no longer fails on its first node for convex models; SOS2 checks catch two nonadjacent nonzeros; constraints with a lower bound of Inf or an upper bound of -Inf are rejected.
  • log(x, base) honors base; powers with exponents 0 and 1 have exact derivatives at zero; t(x) %*% (A %*% x) works.
  • opt_solution_jacobian() requires an optimal termination, the KKT conditions and the second-order sufficient condition, and handles solutions where every variable sits at a bound. Estimated multipliers respect sign restrictions.
  • opt_fixed_relaxation() resolves indicator and SOS constraints at the incumbent. Cone and indicator constructors accept products with parameters. Constraint references from another model are refused. opt_scenarios() validates values. warm_start = FALSE is honored by NLopt and IPOPT. IPOPT options are type checked and rejected options are errors. Exact Z3 coefficients cover subnormal numbers.
  • Local NLP solvers start strictly inside the bounds when no start is given, and stop with a clear message when a function is not finite at the start. NLopt points with NaN are reported as no solution.
  • nlpbb counts nodes without a certified verdict as lost, reports "unknown" instead of infeasible when nodes were lost, catches node errors, and re-solves with integers fixed before accepting a rounded incumbent.
  • Clarabel accepts quadratic objectives with cross terms and returns cone multipliers for models with cones only. ROI loads its plugins itself and passes equality rows correctly.
  • IPOPT: single precision builds fall back to the stub, older IPOPT uses max_cpu_time for time limits, options are tried in the type of the R value first, and callback errors keep their message; a failed trial evaluation is a warning when IPOPT recovers.
  • Curvature tests are relative to the largest eigenvalue and the large matrix Cholesky test shifts only at rounding level. Quadratic rows without finite bounds no longer make a model nonconvex.
  • Matrix indices X[cbind(i, j)] select coordinates. mean() works on expressions. Element names must be unique across blocks.
  • opt_solution_jacobian() checks primal feasibility, refuses abs() at a kink, and treats a point near a bound with a zero multiplier as interior. Row and bound feasibility scale each side by its own bound.
  • Indicator switches must stay binary. opt_fixed_relaxation() refuses a result whose model changed since the solve. Automatic selection skips solvers that cannot reformulate indicator or SOS constraints, and controls a backend ignores are reported in the result warnings.
  • opt_z3_certify() also proves that the reported value is attained, and opt_z3_check() works with nonlinear objectives.
